content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document does today**
- **§ 13 (p0078):** 1-year term auto-renewing for successive one-year periods; *either* party may non-renew on 30 days' notice. Separately, we must arrange a new name server (30 days) / hosting environment (60 days) on discontinuation.
- **§ 14 (p0079):** No express convenience right — it only says TrueLink will keep providing services "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides ... notice of its election to terminate." That implies a Client exit but with a floating 30–60 day tail and no refund mechanic.
- **§ 5 (p0045):** Monthly invoicing in arrears, so refund exposure is limited, but no refund language exists at all.

**Why it deviates**
1. Our convenience right is implicit and imprecise, with no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no confirmation that no penalty applies.
2. Nothing prevents TrueLink from asserting a mid-term convenience exit.
3. TrueLink can drop us at renewal on 30 days' notice — below the playbook's 90-day floor and inconsistent with the 60-day migration burden § 13 places on us.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level)**
- § 14: express Client convenience termination on 30 days' notice, no penalty, refund of prepaid fees; services continue through the effective date; TrueLink has no convenience right during the then-current term.
- § 13: asymmetric non-renewal notice — ours stays at 30 days, TrueLink's moves to 90 days.
